style: Read this as the narrator of a premium technology commercial: warm, confident and inspiring, unhurried, with natural pauses between sentences.

segments.text: Every morning, more than four million people in Abuja ask the same three questions. How much is the fare? When will the bus come? And is this car safe?

Abuja is one of Africa's fastest-growing capitals, adding nearly two hundred thousand people every year. New terminals have been built. Electric and gas-powered buses are arriving. But the system to run them is missing.
segments.source: Growth ~4.6% a year: Macrotrends · Terminals & new fleets: New National Star, WithinNigeria

segments.text: Nigeria's urban mobility and ride-hailing market is worth about four hundred million dollars today, and is forecast to more than double by twenty thirty-one. Yet most daily trips still run on cash, guesswork and trust.
segments.source: Urban mobility & ride-hailing: USD 400M (2025) to USD 965M (2031), Ken Research

segments.text: Commuters can spend up to half their income just getting to work. Owners can't see what their vehicles earn. Government can't see the city move. We are building Tap A Ride because Abuja deserves transport that is fair, safe and visible.
segments.source: Up to half of income on commuting: Daily Trust

segments.text: One platform for everyone. Riders book, and tap to pay, at a fixed fare. Every vehicle is verified. Drivers, operators and fleet owners see every naira. The FCTA sees every route. And Tapi, our AI guide, tells you when to leave.
This is how Africa's cities will move: connected, cashless and smart. Starting in Abuja. Tap A Ride. Know your fare. Know your ride. Just tap.
